home.filmText: A short look at the refinery site, its process units and its product storage.
home.procSub: Every stage is part of a carefully managed industrial refining process.

stages.title: Feedstock reception
stages.text: Furnace Oil, the documented feedstock, is received on site.

stages.title: Storage & handling
stages.text: Feedstock is held in storage tanks and moved by transfer pumps.

stages.title: Preheating & heat recovery
stages.text: Heat exchangers warm the feed, recovering heat from hot product streams.

stages.title: Controlled heating
stages.text: A furnace brings the feed up to temperature before distillation.

stages.title: Vacuum distillation
stages.text: Two Vacuum Distillation Units separate the heavy feed under vacuum.

stages.title: Vacuum generation
stages.text: Steam ejectors create the vacuum the columns operate under.

stages.title: Product separation
stages.text: Separated fractions are drawn off as individual product streams.

stages.title: Storage & dispatch
stages.text: Finished products are stored and dispatched to customers.

about.whoText2: Two Vacuum Distillation Units process Furnace Oil, the documented feedstock. Our products are VDO, LVGO, HVGO and Bitumen.

values.title: Vision
values.text: To achieve operational excellence, strengthen our environmental responsibility, and build positive, sustainable relationships with the community.

values.title: Mission
values.text: To provide high-quality refined petroleum products that meet the growing energy needs of our region and other markets, while ensuring the safety and well-being of our employees, partners, and the communities we serve.

values.title: Our Commitment
values.text: We are committed to providing high-quality petroleum products, strengthening operational excellence, and safeguarding the safety of our employees, partners, and surrounding communities. We also strive to reduce the environmental impact of our operations, develop our capabilities, and strengthen cooperation with local communities, government entities, and industrial partners.

sustainability.title: Refining with responsibility
sustainability.lead: How the refinery manages water, gases, heat and spills across the site.

hr.title: Heat recovery
hr.text: Hot product streams pass their heat to the incoming feed through heat exchangers. The feed arrives at the furnace already preheated, which reduces the heating load on the furnace.
hr.imgAlt: Horizontal heat exchangers at Golden Oil Refinery

sustainability.claimNote: No emissions reductions, energy-saving figures, carbon claims or environmental certifications are stated. They will be added only when documented and approved.

items.title: Water treatment
items.text: Process and site water is treated on site. A dedicated sour water system handles water containing hydrogen sulphide and ammonia, with reverse osmosis and EDI where relevant.

items.title: Flare system
items.text: Excess gases are routed to a flare so they can be handled safely.

items.title: Cooling water recirculation
items.text: Cooling water is recirculated through the cooling towers rather than used once.

items.title: Spill prevention
items.text: Secondary containment is designed to hold spills and keep them from reaching the wider site.

items.title: Oil–water separation
items.text: Oil is separated from water and recovered instead of being lost to the drain.

vacuum.s1p: Heavy feed is separated under deep vacuum, so it boils at far lower temperatures than it would at atmospheric pressure. Scroll to travel inside the column.
vacuum.s2p: Reducing the pressure lowers boiling points and limits thermal cracking of the heavy molecules. The shell opens to show the internals: packed beds, collector trays, the flash zone and the stripping section.
vacuum.s3p: Hot feed enters the flash zone and partly vaporizes. Vapor climbs through the beds while cooler liquid runs down over them; at every surface heat and mass are exchanged, so each level settles at its own boiling range. Steam strips the last light material out of the bottom liquid.
vacuum.lvgoP: The lightest liquid product. It condenses in the upper section and is drawn off a collector tray near the top of the vacuum section.
vacuum.lvgoNote: Typical routing: conversion units or blending, depending on the refinery.
vacuum.hvgoP: A heavier cut, condensed lower in the column and drawn from a second collector tray below the LVGO section.
vacuum.hvgoNote: Typical routing: conversion feed or fuel / lube components, depending on the refinery.
vacuum.resP: The heaviest part of the feed never vaporizes. It collects in the bottom of the column and leaves through the bottom outlet.
vacuum.resNote: Bitumen is made downstream from suitable vacuum residue. It is not drawn directly from the tower.
vacuum.s5: One feed in, three streams out
vacuum.s5p: Illustrative configuration. Real columns differ in internals, sizes and draw-offs from plant to plant.
